rec7Vm5QNrDbc9sdb.Bio: Chance Garton is the host and producer of the Innerverse Podcast, where for over a decade he has investigated consciousness, mythology, symbolism, terrain health, and the psychosomatic language of the human body and mind. A biofield tuning practitioner, he uses tuning forks to help clients resolve physical symptoms, break negative patterns, and return to energetic coherence.
rec7Vm5QNrDbc9sdb.Name: Chance Garton

recBE7KwrPCyVVZMU.Bio: Gabriel, known on air as Slick Dissident, co-hosts InnerVerse's Vibe Rant show and is a longtime recurring guest on the podcast. He teaches occult symbolism and tarot on his YouTube channel, ranging across the Major Arcana, the esoteric Enneagram, mythology and archetype, mystic linguistics, and the symbolism hidden in popular film. He is best known for Tarot-tories, his own system mapping the 22 Major Arcana and zodiac archetypes onto the geography of the United States.
recBE7KwrPCyVVZMU.Name: Gabe (Slick Dissident)
recBE7KwrPCyVVZMU.Role: Co-host of Vibe Rant; teacher of occult symbolism & tarot

recOq9xeYHvqku9Dl.Bio: LC King is a recurring InnerVerse "Vibe Rant" panelist who brings a mechanical/engineering background to discussions of electric-universe theory, cavitation technology, and the intersections of astrology and alchemy.
recOq9xeYHvqku9Dl.Name: LC King

reckIvJxU4wRhybxA.Bio: Mario Garza is the artist and researcher behind Symbolic Studies, a project sharing symbolic insights on the zodiac, mythology, folklore and world religions, with astrology as its foundation. A lifelong artist who has worked as an art director and graphic designer for nearly 25 years, he runs Symbolic Studies from the Pacific Northwest alongside his wife Michelle, who co-hosts the podcast with him. His work traces syncretic threads across tarot, occultism and comparative religion, including the argument that the major deities of antiquity were originally polar gods before a solar model was laid over them. He also offers symbolic birth chart and tarot readings, private lessons and freelance design.
reckIvJxU4wRhybxA.Name: Mario Garza

fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "A Three Hour Slideshow Built on the Cube", "body": "LC King presented a slideshow of about sixty slides that he said he pulled together within a week from years of earlier notes. He argued that horse symbolism led back to a cube, and that the cube pointed to a single central stone or pillar. Chance Garton called the presentation a gift to a podcast host, while Mario Garza and Gabe added tarot, Hebrew letter and wordplay links as each slide appeared. Near the end the group floated taking turns preparing shorter presentations, and LC King said he valued having the others add ideas he might not have seen."}, {"title": "Horse Words, Stars, and Wordplay", "body": "LC King noted that the Latin word for horse, Equus, sits close to equal, eagle and legal in his etymology notes, and he joined horse and eagle in the winged horse Pegasus. Another participant described the square of Pegasus sitting above Pisces and an old Babylonian tradition that treated it as a field between two rivers. Other voices on the panel traded letter switches such as stallion and star, and one of them argued that Mars, mare and the sea shared a root. LC King also offered a personal reading of dark symbolism as the inner stillness of meditation."}, {"title": "Gematria Numbers Around 27 and 216", "body": "LC King broke the word Equus into consonants and vowels and reported values that he tied to 432 and 4320. He argued that 27, 216, 666 and 888 recurred in the geometry of a cube, in musical ratios and in the Earth's equatorial measurements. He also showed that 37 times 27 gave 999 and described 72 as 27 reversed. Another participant linked the number 153 to a fishing net story, and LC King later tied 153 to the vesica piscis shape he drew."}, {"title": "Calendars, Moon Cycles, and Sky Mapping", "body": "LC King argued that multiples of 27 reproduced the synodic cycles of the sun, moon and planets, and that they pointed to a 364 day calendar. He found 364 again in the star names of Orion's belt and in a deck of playing cards with 91 per suit, and he counted the finger segments of the hand to reach 432. He also explained why eight divisions suited sailors better than twelve. Another participant suggested that four horses of different shades could stand for the changing looks of the moon, and a different voice asked how fixed the official planetary figures really were."}, {"title": "Tarot, Hebrew Letters, and the Psychopomp Horse", "body": "Mario Garza said horse symbolism was mercurial, and he tied the horse to the psychopomp role of guiding souls and to the Death card. He said the Hebrew letter Chet, which he gave as meaning canopy, matched the chariot card and its arch shape, and he linked the star Ain to the devil card. Mario also tied the keystone of the Royal Arch and the unicorn horn to the world axis. Gabe said he watched for the hidden yod, and argued that a canted square with a Y in the middle generated a cube."}]
fields.Intro Paragraph 1: The four horsemen of the symbolipocalypse return for a ride through the occult significance of man's trusty steeds. LC King, Mario Garza and Slick Dissident combine their knowledge and powers to decipher the astrotheology, gematria, and mythology of horses. Giddy-up!
